main_text.p: stet[?] substantijs?Hæc profecto naturæ similaritatis omnino repugnant.Neq; præterea tres illæ substantiæ in unum & idem corpus coire possunt,absq; compositione.Propterea corpus ex ijs non erit simplex,nec compositionis expers.Adhæc ex his tribus substantijs unum fieri nequit corpus absq; corporum penetratione, a qua abhorret natura.

Quis præterea os,aut neruum ex substantia carnosa, solida & spirituosa constare dixerit.Nam nulla est huiusmodi partium, quæ tot substantiarum sit particeps.Nulla est igitur pars similaris, quæ substantia solida,carnosa & spirituosa constat. Postmodum ad reliquas rationes,quas producit Fernelius ad suum corroborandum dogma licet pergere. Tria (inquit Eudoxus) cum sint, ex quibus pars unaquæq; similaris constituitur, tria quoque sunt,per quæ vel bene, vel male subsistit, atque conseruatur, quorum unoquoq; pereunte,continuo pars tota perit. Vt autem tria sunt,per quæ pars subsistit: ita & tria sunt, per quæ bene, vel male subsistit:quandoquidem contrariorum eadem est subiecta materia.Illorum trium integritas & moderatio partis est sanitas,eorundem contraria immoderatio,morbus,

page.notes: Left margin: a column of repeated quotation marks (») beside the Eudoxus passage, lines 6 to 15; treated as typographic marks, not transcribed as notes. Words marked [?]: "stet" at the start of the first line is partly cut off and uncertain. The page-number line reads "7" with a superscript "2", transcribed as 72. The catchword "Quo-" stands below the last line, right-aligned. Printed spelling kept, e.g. "Vt", "quoq;", "subiecta", "Adhæc". The line "tria quoque sunt,per quæ vel bene, vel" and the following lines are read from the scan; the exact wording of the first line of the Eudoxus sentence ("quibus pars unaquæq; similaris constituitur") should be checked against the scan.
